He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. ==Early life and high school career== Bryant grew up in [[Riverside, California]] and initially attended [[Fountain Valley High School]], where he was coached by his father D'Cean.{{cite web|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2022/06/24/dcean-bryant-leaves-fountain-valley-to-become-basketball-coach-at-sage-hill/|title=D’Cean Bryant leaves Fountain Valley to become basketball coach at Sage Hill|work=[[Orange County Register]]|date=June 24, 2022|access-date=March 19, 2024}} He transferred to the [[Sage Hill School]] in [[Newport Beach, California]] after his father was hired to coach at the school.{{cite web|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2023/04/05/brandon-benjamin-carter-bryant-shea-joko-win-john-r-wooden-award/|title=Brandon Benjamin, Carter Bryant, Shea Joko win John R. Wooden Award|first=Steve|last=Fryer|work=[[Orange County Register]]|date=April 5, 2023|access-date=March 19, 2024}} Bryant was named the [[Pacific Coast Conference (California)|Pacific Coast Conference]] MVP after averaging 22.1 points, 13.7 rebounds, four assists, 2.9 blocks, and 1.6 steals per game as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/socal/daily-pilot/sports/story/2023-04-07/daily-pilot-boys-basketball-dream-team-carter-bryant-led-sage-hill-to-memorable-season|title=Daily Pilot Boys' Basketball Dream Team: Carter Bryant led Sage Hill to memorable season|work=[[Daily Pilot]]|date=April 7, 2023|access-date=March 19, 2024}} He transferred a second time to [[Centennial High School (Corona, California)|Centennial High School]] in [[Corona, California]] before the start of his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/five-star-arizona-commit-carter-bryant-transferring-from-sage-hill-to-corona-centennial-hs/article_5c4e6c42-f69d-11ed-bbdd-4fa960ee03f9.html|title=Five-star
